reports.title: AST SpaceMobile Provides Business Update and Third Quarter 2026 Results

desk.headline: Revenue nearly tripled to $42.3m but missed; loss per share in line; 2026 revenue goal of $150–200m reaffirmed
results: Revenue rose to $42.3m from $14.7m, split roughly evenly between products ($20.6m) and services ($21.8m), driven by gateway deliveries and US government milestones.
Revenue fell short of the $46.0m estimate; the loss of $0.44 a share was close to the $0.45 expected.
Adjusted operating costs rose to $133.6m from $119.1m in Q2 as engineering work stepped up; reported costs fell because Q2 carried a $125.9m satellite loss.
Cash and restricted cash were $3.2bn, while long-term debt grew to $4.1bn after new convertible note issues.
Japan's J-LEO deal brings about $1.0bn of non-dilutive funding, and a US Space Force contract worth about $100m was won.

guidance.summary: AST said it remains on track for 2026 revenue of $150–200m, with possible upside from new contracts. On the call it also guided Q4 costs and capex higher.

items.metric: Adjusted opex excl. cost of revenue

points: Intermittent nationwide service is due by year-end in the US, Canada, Japan, Saudi Arabia and the UK, with user beta trials in early 2027.
Factories should build six ASIC satellites a month from December; about 45 BlueBirds are targeted in orbit by mid-2027.
Launch deals now cover over 100 satellites for 2027–28; the own Blacklift rocket is planned from late 2028 and adds several hundred million dollars of 2027 capex.
Q4 revenue is expected to be the heaviest of the year; management kept its view of near $1bn revenue in the first year after commercial service starts.
Q3 capex of about $310m was below the $350–425m guide due to timing of launch payments; each satellite including launch costs about $21–23m.
call.source: Press release and presentation (Exhibits 99.1, 99.2) and Investing.com call transcript, 9 Nov 2026

watch: Whether intermittent service actually starts by year-end and the timing of the next SpaceX and Blue Origin launches.
Q4 revenue: about $61–111m is needed to land in the $150–200m range after $88.6m in the first nine months.
Cash burn as Q4 capex rises to $400–500m and Blacklift spending starts.
